newsitem.title: THAILAND: BMW says Rover will show profit in 2000.
newsitem.headline: BMW says Rover will show profit in 2000.

text.p: The chairman of German luxury car maker Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG said on Thursday he still expects Rover Group, which BMW took over in 1994, to report a profit in 2000.
"The year 2000 would be a profit," Bernd Pischetsrieder told Reuters in an interview while in Thailand on a three-nation Asian tour.
"The Rover business has to get better year by year, results will get better year by year. I said this from the beginning."
Over the past few months some industry analysts have said Rover, which BMW bought in an attempt to expand beyond its luxury car base, is in worse financial shape than BMW is admitting.
U.K.-based Rover lost 335 million marks ($227 million) in 1995.
In the first six months of this year, Rover improved its market position with a seven percent increase in vehicle sales, the company said.
Pischetsrieder said BMW has doubled annual investment in Rover and was sure it would prove to be a good investment.
"We knew from the beginning that the existing range of products doesn't allow us to use a large number of components jointly," he said.
"We knew from the beginning the strength Rover had was mainly in the British market which is a very difficult market."
But he said Rover sales had expanded.
"In 1993, Rover sold 55 percent in Britain and now we sell already 55 percent abroad with a (sales) figure which overall is nearly 20 percent higher than 1993."
Salomon Brothers said in a report last month that Rover needed huge amounts of investment from BMW and must streamline its product range.
That report and another article spurred selling in BMW stock in mid-August.
Pischetsrieder said he believed it was fair to expect BMW to report 10 percent profit growth and 4.0 percent increase in sales in 1996.
"Its a fair assessment," he told Reuters in an interview when asked if the company expected full year results to be in line with its six-month figures.
"I would forsee for the rest of the year it will be about the same," he said.
